text:
jess: Heads-up — Acme POC can't complete requests to Private Endpoint, SDK shows TLS client cert error (401) since 08:10 PT.
acme-eng: From our app logs: `tls: handshake failure: no verified client certificate` but curl from our jumpbox with --cert works.
tim: Can you paste an openssl s_client dump from the app host? `openssl s_client -connect priv.redwood.internal:443 -showcerts -state`
acme-eng: Pasted output (trimmed):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Corp CA, CN = Corp Root CA
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=Corp-Proxy-Intercept
   i:/C=US/O=Corp CA/CN=Corp Root CA
---
SSL handshake has read 2345 bytes and written 512 bytes
---
"HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized" after request
```
samir: That shows a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy re-signing the server cert (CN=Corp-Proxy-Intercept). If your proxy terminates TLS and then re-initiates to Redwood, the client cert from the app is not forwarded to us. Redwood's Private Endpoint is configured for mTLS for your org, so we require the original client cert.
jess: Ah — we enabled mTLS on the private endpoint at the start of the POC. Didn't realize their proxy would intercept.
infra-bot: Note: There's a known incompatibility when client-side mTLS is required and outbound traffic is forced through TLS-inspection appliances. See internal KB: pkb/priv-endpoints/mTLS-proxy-compat.
acme-eng: Their network team confirmed they run a transparent HTTPS proxy that performs SSL inspection and does not support client cert passthrough. They also block external OCSP/CRL egress to CA endpoints as outbound is restricted.
tim: Two blocker vectors here: (1) proxy terminates client TLS and drops client cert, and (2) firewall blocks OCSP which can cause server cert validation issues on our side. We need one of:
- Ask Net team to whitelist passthrough for priv.redwood.internal (preferred).
- Or temporarily disable TLS inspection for the POC path.
- Or move POC to dedicated VPN/tunnel that bypasses corporate proxy.
samir: There's a risky workaround where the proxy adds an X-Client-Cert header after validating client cert, but Redwood doesn't accept that pattern for mTLS. We can discuss a signed delegation flow later but not for quick POC.
acme-eng: They'll try a passthrough rule. Also asked if we can relax OCSP checks on our side — not acceptable for prod. For the POC we could allow an escape hatch, but we prefer network change.
jess: If they open passthrough for the endpoint and allow outbound to the CA OCSP URIs (port 80/443 to example-ca.com), we should be good. Can you confirm exact OCSP hosts?
samir: We'll DM a small list of OCSP/CRL endpoints used by our cert chain and a curl snippet to validate from their host. Example: `curl -v https://ocsp.example-ca.com/ocsp` and `openssl s_client -connect priv.redwood.internal:443 -status` to check stapled OCSP.
acme-eng: Updated: network changed to passthrough for priv.redwood.internal and allowed ocsp.example-ca.com outbound. After retest, requests succeed. No more 401s. :white_check_mark:
jess: Great — will log follow-up actions: network should document passthrough for private endpoints using mTLS and we should add a line to the POC checklist about OCSP egress.
tim: Marking as resolved. I'll add a short note to the sales POC playbook with the troubleshooting commands used and the OCSP host list.
infra-bot: Incident note created: poc-1745123456 - root cause: corporate TLS inspection + blocked OCSP. Remediation: passthrough + OCSP egress.
acme-eng: Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick triage.
